main_issue: Whether Agent D may keep his religious red thread on (covered) under the new no-visible-jewellery rule, or must remove it like everyone else before tomorrow's area manager visit.

A-B.evidence: B: 'It should be the same for everyone' (4, 16); A: 'It's the same for everyone. We can't make exceptions' (18); A agrees thread must come off (8).

A-C.evidence: C backs covering (5) and urges A to call or text the manager (25, 27); A refuses 'I'm not calling the manager' (26) and 'My decision is final' (22).

A-D.evidence: A: 'It has to come off' (8, 22); D: 'It stays on' (11), 'Then I can't work tomorrow' (23).

B-C.evidence: C says covering means not visible (5); B objects (4, 14); B resents the text for D (29), C: 'This isn't about you or him' (30).

B-D.evidence: B: 'Covering it isn't the same' (14); D: 'It's not the same thing. This is for my religion' (15); B: 'only a problem because he won't follow the rule' (31).

C-D.evidence: C: 'If he covers it, then it's not visible' (5); D: 'Yeah, exactly' (6); C pushes for the manager to be told (25, 27).
